Name: retrieval_timing_is_budgeting
Title: When to Retrieve Is Only a Budget Question: A Harm-Mass Bound on the Value of Retrieval Timing for Experience Memory, Tested at Two Distractor Levels, With Failure-Keyed Retrieval at Stall Against Planted Recoveries, Coverage-Matched Self Detours and a Compiled Rulebook
Short Hypothesis: With retrieved content, cached prefix and message format held fixed, the value of any retrieval-timing policy (start, fixed schedule, on stall, learned) over always-retrieve is bounded above by the harm mass: the fraction of episodes on which retrieval breaks an episode the static prompt solves, beyond test-retest flips. On ALFWorld we measure the harm mass as a paired-table estimand at two distractor levels of one expert bank and predict it is inside the +/-8 floor at the natural bank and above it with mislabelled twins. Stall-triggered retrieval then sits within the floor of always-retrieve at the natural bank in both directions, overall and on the rows where the trigger fires, and re-delivering the already-read block at the stall adds nothing; at the twin bank it gains over a separately run always-retrieve replicate by at least 8 net but never more than the harm mass plus the floor, and solves no episodes beyond test-retest that neither the static prompt nor the start read solves, so timing re-trades uncached tokens for the same success and cannot buy more. A failure-keyed query at stall beats a content-free key only when the bank holds matching recoveries: at matched coverage the agent's own curated detours do as well as planted recoveries, the natural self pool does not, and a compiled recovery rulebook in the cached prefix matches planted retrieval at zero uncached cost.
Related Work: arXiv:2607.24010 (When Should Active RAG Retrieve?) recasts active retrieval as marginal correctness over the no-retrieval answer under a budget, but on QA with document retrieval, without a harm-mass estimand on paired seeds, a stall trigger or caching costs. ProactAgent (arXiv:2604.20572, 'Ask Only When Needed') retrieves proactively from memory and skills for lifelong agents without an always-retrieve-at-matched-content arm or an upper bound on the decision. FLARE (arXiv:2305.06983) and Adaptive-RAG (arXiv:2403.14403) trigger retrieval by uncertainty or complexity in QA. Reflexion (arXiv:2303.11366) conditions on failure across trials, not within-episode stalls, and has no static control. Digest: arXiv:2607.07380 (hidden-state uncertainty decides when to retrieve; no always/never baselines), s2:93def179dbebdaf187c0bce1f494a2bbd39ddc19 (RL proxy decides when/how; cost unaccounted), arXiv:2510.16724 (survey; no common protocol), arXiv:2607.20972 (cue-triggered deterministic injection beats voluntary reads; no harm bound or compiled control), arXiv:2505.00234 (self-generated examples for sequential decision tasks, the on-policy bank). Archived ideas do not address timing; compile_dont_retrieve concerns the goal-conditioned read at episode start.
Abstract: Adaptive retrieval papers ask when to retrieve but do not report what a perfect answer to that question would be worth. For experience memory under prompt caching the accounting is simple: with the retrieved content, the cached prefix and the message format held fixed, a timing policy can add success over always-retrieve only on episodes where retrieval breaks an episode the static prompt would have solved. We call that fraction the harm mass and measure it as a pre-registered paired-table estimand on ALFWorld (Qwen3-32B, 274 games x 2 seeds, static3 cached prefix from Measurement C, one k=3 goal-keyed block appended at step 0 or later): P(static succeeds and retrieval fails) minus the same discordance between two static runs, at two distractor levels of one expert bank (natural, and a 1:1 mislabelled-twin bank in which goal-keyed retrieval returns a wrong-type trajectory in about half the slots). Predictions: the harm mass is inside the +/-8 floor at the natural bank and above it with twins; stall-triggered retrieval (two consecutive 'Nothing happens' or a repeated action) is within the floor of always-retrieve at the natural bank in both directions, overall and on the rows where the trigger fires, and re-delivering the already-read block at the stall adds nothing; at the twin bank it gains over a separately run always-retrieve replicate by at least 8 net and by no more than the harm mass plus the floor, with the bound estimated from the other replicate so bound and gain cannot co-move, and the late-read-only mass (episodes the stall arm solves that neither the static prompt nor the start read solves, beyond test-retest) stays inside the floor; a fixed step-10 schedule does the same as the trigger. We then ask whether the query at stall matters, separating key from content in a k=1 2x2 (failure key vs random key; planted-recovery bank vs expert pool) and manipulating recovery coverage in the agent's own detour pool (natural coverage measured by a validated tagger; curated recovery windows at coverage near 1). Predictions: the failure key beats a random key only with planted recoveries; curated self detours match planted recoveries at matched coverage while the natural pool falls short; and a ~200-token recovery rulebook in the cached prefix matches planted retrieval at zero uncached cost. The output is an accuracy-cost frontier on which the timing decision moves along the frontier rather than above it, with the bound tested as an inequality at a level where it binds, the one channel that could breach it measured directly, and a test of whether any query is more than decorative at stall time.
Experiments: Setting as in Measurement A/C: ALFWorld 274 games x 2 seeds, identical game seeds across arms, Qwen3-32B on two vLLM replicas with prefix caching. Shared prefix: static3 (3 fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars, ~430 tokens, cached), Measurement C's best static arm; every arm sits on it. Retrieval block: k=3 goal-keyed items (~430 tokens) appended as one environment-style message with identical text and format at step 0 (always), step 10 (schedule), the stall (stall arms) or both (double-read), so content, prefix and format are fixed and only the delivery step varies. Banks: natural expert bank; distractor bank = expert bank plus one mislabelled twin per item (its goal sentence attached to the trajectory of a different-type expert item sharing the target object), so goal-keyed retrieval ties twins with originals and returns a wrong-type trajectory in about half the k=3 slots; planted-recovery bank (five ALFWorld failure modes: closed receptacle, wrong receptacle, object already held, wrong object instance, missing 'go to'; one ~40-token recovery item each, keyed by failure text; coverage 1.0 by construction); self pool = 1,892 self-generated successes with detours, indexed by failed-action windows (natural level), and its curated subset of windows the tagger marks as a failure mode followed by a recovery within three steps (curated level); coverage and tagger validation under Baselines. Stall trigger: first occurrence of two consecutive 'Nothing happens' or a repeated (observation, action) pair; firing is fixed by the static3 trajectory before any read, so a stall arm's firing rows are outcome-blind. Queries at stall: goal sentence (k=3, matching always); failure key = last three actions and observations (k=1); random key = uniform draw from the pool (k=1); k=1 wherever the one-item-per-mode planted bank is a comparator. Estimands Delta_harm(L) and Lambda(L) are defined under P1 and P6 (static3_A = the Measurement C cell, static3_B = a fresh re-run); the cross-fitted oracle is descriptive only, no cell. Cells (548 episodes each; ~30 min on one replica, two cells concurrently): (1) static3_B; (2) always-natural; (3) always-distractor_A; (3b) always-distractor_B, a second separately sampled run on the same game seeds (as static3_B is to static3_A), the comparator for P6's gain so that bound (from cell 3) and gain share no run; (4) stall goal-key k=3, natural; (5) stall goal-key k=3, distractor; (6) step-10 schedule, natural; (6b) double-read natural: the block at step 0 and the identical block again at the stall (the goal-keyed analogue of cell 13); (7) stall failure-key k=1, expert pool; (8) stall failure-key k=1, planted; (9) stall random-key k=1, planted; (10) stall failure-key k=1, self natural; (11) stall failure-key k=1, self curated; (12) static3 + recovery rulebook (the five planted items concatenated, ~200 tokens, cached; the planted bank's whole-bank arm); (13) rulebook + stall failure-key k=1 planted. Optional: (14) curated-self whole-bank arm, cached, truncated to the top-N recovery windows by tag confidence, type-balanced, that fit 16k with the longest trajectory (exploratory). The threshold-5 cell is cut. Arithmetic: 15 confirmatory cells x 548 = 8,220 episodes, ~3.75 h wall on two A100s; with cell 14, 8,768 episodes, ~4.0 h, inside the 4 h envelope; cells 3b and 5 (0.5 h) run only if P1 finds Delta_harm(distractor) >= 8. Logged per episode and arm: success, steps, firing step, uncached prefill tokens (prompt minus cached tokens from vLLM), cache hit rate; accuracy vs uncached tokens per episode is the cost axis. Pre-registered order: 1-3 (P1 decides whether the distractor level exists), 4, 6, 6b (P2), 3b, 5 (P6), 8, 9, 7 (P3), 10-11 (P4), 12-13 (P5), 14.
Baselines and Ablations: Baselines: never-retrieve = static3 (cached; the best static arm from Measurement C, +12.4 over k0); always-retrieve = static3 plus the same k=3 goal-keyed block appended at step 0 (uncached block, ~430 tokens per episode; its residual over static3_B is checked against Measurement C's +17.2 +/- 5); always-distractor replicate (cell 3b, separately sampled; the independent comparator for P6's gain, with the bound taken from cell 3); fixed step-10 schedule (timing without a trigger); double-read (cell 6b: always plus the identical block again at the stall; the delivery-position control for the goal-keyed block, the analogue of rulebook + retrieval); random-key-at-stall on the planted bank (content-free key, pool fixed); failure-key-at-stall on the expert pool (key fixed, no recovery content); compiled recovery rulebook in the cached prefix (the static counterpart of planted retrieval and the whole-bank arm of the 5-item planted bank); curated-self whole-bank arm (cached, truncated; optional); cross-fitted oracle (decide on static3_A, score static3_B where it succeeded and always elsewhere; descriptive upper bound, no cell). Whole-bank rule: the expert bank exceeds the ~80-item whole-context limit; its truncated whole-bank arm is Measurement C's k-sweep (k7 = +19.5 over static3) and the start read is held at k=3 here. Why the twin bank should harm: Measurement C's wrong-type placebo blind1 is -3 under k0 and about -15 under static3. Coverage c(pool) = fraction of stall-firing episodes (cell 4's log) whose tagged failure mode has a same-mode recovery window in the pool; the rule-based tagger reads the last three actions and observations and is validated on 100 hand-labelled stall windows (agreement >= 0.8) before the self-pool cells run. Type conditioning: every arm shares the static3 prefix, so type conditioning is constant in every contrast; the rulebook and planted items are keyed by failure mode, not task type; Measurement C's instr_all (type-agnostic, -20.1 under k3) and blind1 (wrong type) are the standing references. Manipulated properties, two levels each on one environment: distractor rate of the expert bank (natural vs 1:1 mislabelled twins) for the harm mass; recovery coverage of the self pool (natural c_nat vs curated c_cur, both measured) for the failure key. Ablations and analyses: rulebook with vs without stall retrieval on top (P5); always with vs without the stall re-read (P2c); step-10 schedule vs stall trigger (P2 secondary); the firing-row subset contrast (P2b) and the late-read-only estimand Lambda (P6, and descriptively at the natural bank), both computed from existing cells.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (harm mass small at the natural bank, large with twins): Delta_harm(L) = P(static3_A succeeds, always(L) fails) - P(static3_A succeeds, static3_B fails) on the 548 paired rows; always(L) = cell 2 or 3. Prediction: Delta_harm(natural) < 8, Delta_harm(distractor) >= 8. Falsified if Delta_harm(natural) >= 8 (timing has headroom; producible: Measurement C's look-at is +4.8 with CI including 0 and pick types +10 to +12, so 8 to 12 points of harm there is reachable) or Delta_harm(distractor) < 8 (the reader ignores twins; P6 not run).
- P2 (timing is budgeting at the natural bank; two-sided, undiluted): (a) stall goal-key (cell 4) within +/-8 net of always-natural (cell 2); (b) on cell 4's firing rows (outcome-blind; cell 2 scored on the same rows), within the subset-scaled floor 8 x sqrt(548/n_fire), about 11 at n_fire = 274; (c) double-read (cell 6b) minus cell 2 below 8 net. Falsified below the floor in (a) or (b): the stall arrives after the budget is spent. Falsified above it in (b): the same items read after exploration beat them read at start where both read, value Delta_harm(natural) < 8 cannot supply; or in (c): re-delivering content already in context adds 8 net, a delivery-position channel beyond harm avoidance. (b) and (c) are undiluted by non-firing rows. Secondary: step-10 schedule (cell 6) within +/-8 of cell 4, falsified if more than 8 below.
- P6 (headline; the bound where it binds; run only if Delta_harm(distractor) >= 8): G = success(cell 5) - success(cell 3b, the separately sampled always-distractor replicate) lies in [8, Delta_harm(distractor) + 8], the bound from cell 3 alone so bound and gain share no run; and Lambda = P(cell 5 succeeds, static3_A fails, cell 3 fails) - P(static3_B succeeds, static3_A fails, cell 3 fails) (late-read-only mass) is below 8. Falsified if G > Delta_harm(distractor) + 8 or Lambda >= 8: the stall arm solves, beyond test-retest, episodes neither the static prompt nor the start read solves, the only channel that can breach the bound (producible if exemplars read after exploration apply to the located object or a late-read twin is ignored where an early one derails; with P(static3 fails, always-distractor fails) near 25 percent, Lambda = 8 is one late-read success in three). Falsified if G < 8: the trigger also fires on static-solved episodes, so the harm avoidance is not realized.
- P3 (failure key needs matching content; key and pool separated): at stall, k=1, failure-key planted (cell 8) exceeds random-key planted (cell 9; key varies, pool fixed) and failure-key expert pool (cell 7; pool varies, key fixed), each by at least 8 net. Falsified if either gap is below 8: the first means the failure text does not index the recovery or the reader ignores a 40-token hint mid-episode (random-key hits the right item on 20 percent of firings); the second means expert segments already carry the recovery. If the first fails, P4 and P5 are uninterpretable.
- P4 (self-pool coverage manipulated): natural self pool (cell 10, c_nat measured) and curated pool (cell 11, recovery-tagged windows; c_cur expected >= 0.8), failure key, k=1, against cell 8. Prediction: curated within +/-8 net of planted; natural at least 8 below curated. Falsified if curated is more than 8 below planted (own detours unusable even when present) or natural within +/-8 of curated (the natural pool already delivers recoveries by the failure key). Guard: if c_nat >= 0.8 the clause is scored as natural vs planted (falsified if within +/-8); if c_cur < 0.8 the curated clause is exploratory.
- P5 (rulebook matches retrieval; conditional on P3's first clause): static3 + rulebook (cell 12) within +/-8 net of cell 8, and rulebook + planted stall retrieval (cell 13) below 8 net over cell 12. Falsified if cell 8 beats cell 12 by 8 or more (recovery must arrive at the moment of failure) or cell 13 exceeds cell 12 by 8 or more (delivery position adds value with content already in the prefix). Content identical by construction.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired (game, seed) rows with identical game seeds across arms; primary outcome task success; net differences with cluster-bootstrap CIs over 274 games; +/-8-net floor pre-registered at 274 x 2, scaled by sqrt(548/n) for the pre-registered firing-row subset (exploratory below n = 200); margins as fractions of the Measurement C retrieval gain (+17.2, CI half-width about 5). Delta_harm(L) and Lambda(L) are pre-registered paired-table estimands with the static3_A vs static3_B test-retest term subtracted, each with a cluster-bootstrap CI, compared with thresholds and never with a cell they are built from; McNemar discordant cells reported alongside; no oracle cell; Lambda at the natural bank (cells 4, 2) is reported descriptively beside P2. Replicates: static3_B (cell 1) calibrates static test-retest (D0); always-distractor_B (cell 3b) is a second separately sampled run so that P6's bound (from cell 3) and gain (against cell 3b) share no run, and P(cell 3 succeeds, cell 3b fails) is reported as the always-arm test-retest term, expected close to D0. Positive controls that must clear the floor before any null is read: always-natural minus static3_B >= +8 (expected +17.2 +/- 5; a shortfall is reported against that value); Delta_harm(distractor) >= 8 before cells 3b and 5; P3's planted gain >= 8 before P4 and P5. Shared cells disclosed: cell 2 enters Delta_harm(natural) and P2(a), (b), (c), so its noise moves P1's falsifier and P2's upper falsifiers together; cell 3 enters Delta_harm(distractor) and Lambda(distractor) as a conditioning event but not P6's gain; cell 8 anchors P3, P4 and P5, with P4 and P5 gated on P3. Firing-row subset for P2(b): cell 4's own trigger log (outcome-blind, fixed before the read), applied to cell 2 on the same rows; it conditions on a stall in cell 4 and on nothing in cell 2, which tilts (b) toward its lower falsifier, so the double-read contrast (c), scored on all rows, carries the upper test symmetrically. Stall arms log firing rate and step-at-fire; the pre-registered expectation is firing on at most 50 percent of episodes, and a higher rate is a detector-selectivity failure reported on the cost axis, not a falsifier. Tagger validated on 100 hand-labelled stall windows (agreement >= 0.8) before the self-pool cells; c_nat, c_cur and the confusion matrix reported. Cost is uncached prefill tokens per episode from vLLM logs (the double-read arm pays the block twice on firing rows and sits to the right of always on the cost axis); cache hit rate verified for static3, rulebook and whole-bank arms. P1-P6 and the cell order pre-registered before cell 1; per-type numbers and cell 14 are exploratory.

Risk Factors and Limitations: The mislabelled-twin bank may not produce harm if the reader ignores wrong-type trajectories (Delta_harm(distractor) < 8); then the high level is unavailable and P6 is not run, which is reported; a second construction (wrong-type items with rewritten goals) is the next attempt and is out of this budget. The stall definition is heuristic; if it fires on more than half the episodes the cost saving is lost while the accuracy prediction still stands; the step budget may make late retrieval useless (P2's lower falsifier, itself informative); the firing-row contrast has a wider floor and a selection asymmetry that is disclosed, which is why the double-read cell also carries P2's upper test. The double-read arm pays the block twice on firing rows, so it sits to the right of always on the cost axis; it tests delivery position, not cost. The always-distractor replicate buys independence of bound and gain at the price of one cell; if run-to-run variation is very small the replicate is close to cell 3, which does not reintroduce co-movement (they remain separate samples) but makes the always-arm test-retest term small, and it is reported either way. The failure-mode tagger may be unreliable on some modes; its agreement is gated before the self-pool cells. The self pool's recovery windows may be too rare for some modes (c_cur < 0.8), in which case the curated level is not coverage-matched to the planted bank and P4's curated clause is exploratory. ALFWorld has only five recurring failure modes, which favours the rulebook; this is the claim but limits generality, and WebShop (different failure modes, a day of setup) is the stated extension. The cross-fitted oracle uses outcome information and is descriptive, not deployable. vLLM seed reproducibility is imperfect; static3_B quantifies it and it is subtracted from Delta_harm and Lambda. Learned timing policies are not trained; the claim is that no policy with the same content can exceed the harm mass, tested on stall, schedule and double-read policies at two harm levels.
Addresses gap: G14 (value of the retrieval decision quantified against always-retrieve, never-retrieve, a fixed schedule and a double read at accounted per-episode cost, with a harm-mass upper bound measured at two distractor levels, tested where it binds against an independent replicate, and the late-read-only channel that could breach it measured directly); secondary G15 (whether a failure-keyed query is more than decorative depends on measured recovery coverage, planted, curated-self and natural, and whether compiled instructions match it).
Not a restatement of: Brief bullet 'Retrieval on this node (Measurement A): k=0 0.536/0.549 -> k=3 0.807/0.869' and Measurement C's k3 - static3 = +17.2 measure always-retrieve at start; this idea claims the value of any timing decision with the same content is bounded by a quantity those cells cannot see (the mass of static-solved episodes that retrieval breaks, beyond test-retest), measures it as a paired-table estimand, and manipulates it with a distractor bank so the bound is tested as an inequality rather than as a null. Digest card arxiv:2607.07380 decides when to retrieve from hidden-state uncertainty without always/never baselines; this idea claims and tests that no decision policy can beat always-retrieve by more than the measured harm mass, and that the failure key's value tracks measured recovery coverage (planted, curated-self, natural) and is compilable into a cached rulebook. None of the four archived ideas concerns timing; compile_dont_retrieve addresses the goal-conditioned read at start, which is held fixed at k=3 on the static3 prefix here; distractor rate and recovery coverage are manipulated, not named.
Changes made: Round 2 (entailment check r2). P6 (headline, near_entailed): both named fixes taken. The gain is now scored against an independent always-distractor replicate (new cell 3b, a separately sampled run on the same game seeds) while the bound Delta_harm(distractor) is computed from cell 3 alone, so bound and gain share no run and cannot co-move; and the direct late-read-only estimand Lambda = P(stall succeeds, static3_A fails, always fails) minus its static3_B test-retest analogue is added with its own falsifier (Lambda >= 8), the producible mechanisms named and the base rate stated (P(static3 fails, always-distractor fails) near 25 percent); Lambda is also reported at the natural bank. P2 (open, but upper side nearly closed by mixture dilution): both named fixes taken. (b) a pre-registered firing-row contrast, stall vs always on the rows where cell 4's outcome-blind trigger fires, with the floor scaled by sqrt(548/n_fire) and exploratory below n = 200; (c) a double-read cell (new cell 6b: block at step 0 and again at the stall) whose gain over always must stay below 8 net on all rows; the selection asymmetry of (b) is disclosed and (c) carries the upper test symmetrically. P1, P3, P4, P5: unchanged in substance; wording compressed to bring Experiments and Falsifiable Predictions under the 4,000-character limits. Budget: the optional threshold-5 cell is cut; 15 confirmatory cells x 548 = 8,220 episodes, ~3.75 h wall, plus optional cell 14 to ~4.0 h; cells 3b and 5 run only if P1 finds the distractor level, so the natural-bank programme costs 3.25 h. Novelty kept: the bound is still tested as an inequality at the level where it binds, now against an independent comparator and with the only channel that can breach it measured directly, which makes the headline more refutable, not safer; no clause was hedged, no target dropped, and the 'natural self pool is decorative' clause stays.
